_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: Two companies say trucks with nobody at the wheel are running between Dallas and Houston. The state permission they need carries no fee, does not expire and can't ask for crash history.

introduction.text: Kodiak AI says it will [launch unsupervised long-haul driverless service on the Dallas-Houston freight lane by the end of 2026](c22). It says it [now consistently completes deliveries between its Lancaster, Texas, hub and its launch destination in Houston without human intervention](c23). A safety observer still rides along, and the company says [the safety observer never touched the wheel, including on surface streets](c24).

Two days earlier Aurora held its investor day in Dallas, and its release said [Attendees will have the opportunity to ride in Aurora Driver-powered trucks, without a person behind the wheel](c28) on part of the same route. Aurora says it is [fully allocated to exit the year with 200 driverless trucks in operation](c29). Those figures are the companies' own. None of them is a finding by any agency.

paragraphs.text: Texas has required a permission for this since late spring. The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles says it plainly. [All companies operating automated vehicles commercially on or after May 28, 2026, are required to maintain an active authorization with TxDMV.](c1) Commercial activity means moving [property or passengers in furtherance of a commercial enterprise on Texas roads without a human driver](c3).

The application is a set of acknowledgements. The first says the truck is [Capable of operating in compliance with applicable traffic and motor vehicle laws of this state](c5). The next says it is [Equipped with a required recording device](c6), and that its driving system is [in compliance with applicable federal law](c7). The company also affirms the truck is [Capable of achieving a minimal risk condition](c8) if that system fails, that it is [Registered and titled in accordance with the laws of this state](c9) and that it is insured. It also certifies that the Department of Public Safety has a plan for how emergency responders [should interact with the automated motor vehicle](c11).
The department states the terms plainly. [No fees are required for an authorization to operate automated vehicles. Authorizations do not expire and are valid until revoked by the department.](c12)

sections.heading: What the state can't ask for

paragraphs.text: When the department wrote its rules, the City of Dallas asked for more. [The City of Dallas encourages the department to require robust safety documentation, including crash history and proof of community stakeholder coordination, and to make information about approved operators publicly accessible.](c18)

The department answered that the law gave it no room. It wrote that [Transportation Code, § 545.453 and § 545.456 do not allow the department to require authorization holders to submit crash history or proof of community stakeholder coordination](c19). Whether it publishes information about operators, it said, [is based on statutory confidentiality requirements in Government Code, Chapter 552](c20). So a truck has to carry a recorder, and the state that authorizes it can't require the operator to hand over its crash history.

The department sets its line at serious harm. [The operation of an automated motor vehicle is considered to endanger the public when the operation has resulted, or is likely to result, in serious bodily injury as defined by Section 1.07, Texas Penal Code.](c13) Below that line the department says so directly. [The department is unlikely to take administrative enforcement action](c14) in those cases.

Once it acts, the operator has a path back. [An authorization holder has 10 days to request that a final decision be reviewed by the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH).](c15) The department then files within {{number:c16}} days and [the hearing must be held within 60 days of the request filed by the department](c16). [If the hearing is not held within the required time, then the authorization is immediately reinstated.](c17)

A concern about a driverless truck behaving in a way that could hurt someone goes to the department's Enforcement Division through its motor carrier credentialing site at txmccs.txdmv.gov. The same site is where law enforcement checks whether a vehicle or its operator holds an authorization. The record carries this authorization as its own entry and will note when the department acts under it.

sections.heading: What this edition does not establish

paragraphs.text: It does not establish which companies hold an authorization today, because the department's lookup was not read. The count of trucks now on the road comes only from Breitbart's account of a CNBC ride, which puts Aurora at [20 driverless trucks now](c34). Kodiak and Waabi give different lengths for the same corridor, [219 miles apart along Interstate 45](c25) and [roughly 240 miles](c33), and this edition does not choose between them. The sensor kit and the cab in the visual edition are illustrative and are not any one company's hardware.
